questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Seychelles?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Seychelles article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Seychelles?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Seychelles on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Seychelles article.

questions.proof: Other nearby island countries and territories include Zanzibar to the west, Mauritius, Rodrigues, Agalega and Réunion to the south, and Comoros and Mayotte to the southwest.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Seychelles?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Seychelles article.

questions.proof: The official languages are Creole, English, and French.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “There are small minorities of immigrants from Europe, China and _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “China”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Seychelles article.

questions.proof: There are small minorities of immigrants from Europe, China and India.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Seychelles and the islands to the south, _____ and Mauritius, all had legal slavery and were part of the slave trade.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “south”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Seychelles article.

questions.proof: Seychelles and the islands to the south, Madagascar and Mauritius, all had legal slavery and were part of the slave trade.
